page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical AMD EPYC 9T24 core operating at 2.7 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core performance, placing in the top 25% for both stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. However, due to its low core count of 2 vCPUs, multi-core performance is weak, ranking in the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is average, while read-only small block memory bandwidth is poor. Database operations and Redis SET operations also score in the bottom 10%, indicating limitations under high-throughput transactional workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r8a.large offers a high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The primary tradeoff is the limited multi-core scaling and poor database transaction performance. It is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive applications, single-threaded processing tasks, caching layers with moderate throughput requirements, and basic web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.large is a memory-optimized virtual server featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, running on an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides 8.0 GB of memory per core but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark data shows strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% in Geekbench and stress-ng tests. Conversely, multi-core performance, database operations, and Redis throughput are weak to poor due to the dual-vCPU limitation. With a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, this instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-effective for memory-sensitive, low-concurrency workloads. It is best suited for lightweight caching, single-threaded tasks, and moderate web serving.
